summary: [Network Seminar] [Online] - ECE/RBCCPS/CNI -- February 24, 2026 -- Quantum Communication Advantage for Leader Election and Agreement
description:
Dear All,

Networks Seminar, supported by the Centre for Networked Intelligence, is a technical discussion forum in topics including but not limited to computer networks, machine learning, signal processing, and information theory. The seminar series has a webpage hosted at https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/.

You are invited to the following seminar held as part of this series.

Title:  Quantum Communication Advantage for Leader Election and Agreement

Speaker: Prof. Gopal Pandurangan, Moores Professor, University of Houston, USA

Time: 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM (IST)

Date: 24 February 2026

Venue: Online on Zoom

Zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/83388976389?pwd=XcpO3GhLxsR14a7SVbPx33HQQa1jbt.1

Zoom Meeting ID: 833 8897 6389, Pass Code: NSSIISc

YouTube Livestream:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uq70ojiD-Ww

Webpage Link: https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-02-24/

Abstract: This talk posits a new quantum framework for designing and analyzing communication-efficient distributed quantum algorithms. Using this framework, we present distributed quantum algorithms for two fundamental problems in distributed computing, namely, leader election and agreement. Our quantum algorithms are significantly more message-efficient compared to their classical counterparts and breach the classical lower bounds. Joint work with Fabien Dufoulon (Lancaster University) and Frédéric Magniez (Université Paris Cité, CNRS, IRIF).

Bio: Gopal Pandurangan is a Moores Professor of Computer Science at the University of Houston, USA. His research interests include the theory and algorithms for distributed computing, networks, quantum computing, machine learning, and big data, and he has over 150 refereed publications. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), a recipient of the University of Houston Research Excellence Award, and a winner of the ACM PODC 2025 Best Paper Award.
More details: https://sites.google.com/site/gopalpandurangan/


ALL ARE WELCOME.

Thank you,
CNI Seminar Series Organizing Committee.

summary: [Network Seminar] [Hybrid] - ECE/RBCCPS/CNI -- February 25, 2026 -- What Can Be Recovered Under Sparse Adversarial Corruption? Assumption-free Theory for Linear Measurements
description:
Dear All,

Networks Seminar, supported by the Centre for Networked Intelligence, is a technical discussion forum in topics including but not limited to computer networks, machine learning, signal processing, and information theory. The seminar series has a webpage hosted at https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/.

You are invited to the following seminar held as part of this series.

Title: What Can Be Recovered Under Sparse Adversarial Corruption? Assumption-free Theory for Linear Measurements

Speaker: Prof. Alexandre Reiffers, Associate Professor, IMT Atlantique

Time: 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM (IST)

Date: 25 February 2026

Venue: GJ Hall and Online on Zoom

Zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/83388976389?pwd=XcpO3GhLxsR14a7SVbPx33HQQa1jbt.1

Zoom Meeting ID: 833 8897 6389, Pass Code: NSSIISc

YouTube Livestream: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NL5fzt-57OM

Webpage Link: https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-02-25/  <https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-02-25/>

Abstract: Let $\bA\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be an arbitrary, known matrix and $\be$ a $q$-sparse adversarial vector. Given $\by=\bA\xS+\be$ and $q$, we seek the smallest robust solution set containing $\xS$ that is uniformly recoverable from $\by$ without knowing $\be.$  While exact recovery of $\xS$ via strong (and often impractical) structural assumptions on $\bA$ or $\xS$ (e.g., restricted isometry, sparsity) is well studied, recoverability for arbitrary $\bA$ and $\xS$ remains open. Our main result shows that the smallest robust solution set is $\xS + \ker(\bU), $  where $\bU$ is the unique projection matrix onto the intersection of rowspaces of all possible submatrices of $\bA$ obtained by deleting $2q$ rows. Moreover, we prove that every $\bx$ that minimizes the $\ell_0$-norm of $\by - \bA \bx$ lies in $\xS + \ker(\bU)$, which then gives a constructive approach to recover this set.

Bio: Alexandre Reiffers-Masson has developed a research trajectory grounded in applied mathematics, optimisation, and learning, with a strong connection to real-world systems and industrial applications. After completing his PhD at Inria on game-theoretic models applied to online social networks, he worked as a research engineer at SafranTech, where he studied predictive maintenance policy strategies using stochastic models and reliability theory. From 2018-2020, he pursued a postdoctoral position at IISc Bangalore India, focusing on information design and decision-making in IoT and industrial systems. Since joining IMT Atlantique as associate professor, in March 2020, his research has focused on adversarial learning and distributed learning for network robustness, fault detection using machine learning (time-series segmentation and Novel class discovery), stochastic processes for the study of distributed ledgers and stochastic optimisation problems for resource allocation problems in cloud, defence and cyber-security. He is also the coordinator of two international projects that bridge AI, distributed systems, and security.
More details: https://sites.google.com/view/alexandre-reiffers/about
